title: [France] train_s1: digit structure and address-number behaviour
filename_discrepancy: tasks/P031.json names P031_France_train_s1_numeric.md; the work order mandates P031_France_train_s1_digits.md. Followed the work order.
profile_input: analysis_out/profile/train_s1.json (+ train_s2, train_s3, test_s1, test_s2, test_s3 for cross-source contrast)
headline: The France slice of train_s1 is EMPTY: country_rows has no France key, France share is exactly 0 of 2,206,821, and every France rate in this work order is UNDEFINED (0/0), not 0%. The real substance is the PIN question, and it now CLOSES: pin is dead code in EVERY country because nums.append() at normalize.py:340 runs outside the guard, so every number already reaches anums and the kind-2 blocking keys regardless of pin.

france_train_s1.arithmetic: country_rows holds only US=1323633 and India=883188; 1323633+883188 = 2206821 = rows exactly, so the breakdown is complete and France is absent, not zero-valued.
france_train_s1.mechanism: build_profile.py:62 builds country_rows as a Counter; line 142 emits dict(country_rows). A country with zero rows produces NO KEY AT ALL, not a zero entry.

all_requested_france_train_stats.reason: Each is f(France)/rows(France) with rows(France)=0. 0/0 is undefined. Publishing any as 0% would assert that 0 France rows lacked the feature, when the truth is that no France rows were observed. Reading a zero-denominator artifact as a rate is the exact error behind the retracted '100% of France rows resolve a state' figure.

pin_verdict.verdict: DEAD CODE IN EVERY COUNTRY. Not a lost signal anywhere. The entire pin thread should be closed; leave the guard alone.
pin_verdict.argument_a_never_populated_for_US_or_Fra: normalize.py:337 requires country == 'India', so pin == '' by construction for 100% of US and France rows.
pin_verdict.argument_b_essentially_never_populated_f: pin fires only on a standalone 6-digit number. Total India dig6 across ALL SIX files = 2237 occurrences in 10,544,085 India rows = 0.000212/row (0.0212%). Indian PINs are 6 digits, yet essentially no Indian address in this dataset carries one.
pin_verdict.argument_c_redundant_even_when_it_fires: normalize.py:340 nums.append(n2) sits OUTSIDE the len==6/country=='India' guard, so EVERY number of EVERY length in EVERY country is appended to nums. That flows to (i) prep.py:16 anums -> features.py:98-99 qm/sm/qm1/sm1 -> num1_eq, m_inter, m_cont; and (ii) atoks (normalize.py:345-346 t.isdigit()) -> keys.py:39-41 nums = tokens matching ^\d+$ -> kind-2 (AA) blocking keys at keys.py:63,65. So a 5- or 6-digit number is already a model feature AND already a blocking key, with or without pin.
pin_consumers_exactly_two: prep.py:17 -> pin column -> keys.py:44,58 : string 'pin'+pin becomes one extra kind-0 (name x address) blocking key
features.py:100,114 -> pin_eq : one ternary feature, already established at 0.0% of rows by the fleet brief

india_dig6_all_files.note: The total population that can ever set pin != ''. dig6 is lookaround-guarded.

us_dig6_source_asymmetry.note: Quantified per source file as instructed. The ASYMMETRY IS REAL; its 'pin' INTERPRETATION is wrong.

us_dig5_per_row_is_flat.conclusion: The source-1/2-3 asymmetry is ISOLATED TO 6 DIGITS and does not touch 5 digits. pin is the only consumer keyed on 6-digit length and it is redundant anyway, so the asymmetry costs nothing.

are_us_5_digit_values_house_numbers_or_z.verdict: HOUSE NUMBERS, NOT ZIPs. CONFIRMED by a counting argument that needs no positional data.
are_us_5_digit_values_house_numbers_or_z.claim_being_verified: The earlier finding said US 5-digit values are house numbers, not ZIPs.
are_us_5_digit_values_house_numbers_or_z.method: addr_tokens is the top 4000 per country. Read the actual rank-4000 cutoff, then count how many pure 5-digit and 6-digit tokens reach it. A ZIP field would be present in essentially every address and is strongly concentrated, so it would saturate the top-4000 list.
are_us_5_digit_values_house_numbers_or_z.key_arithmetic: US train_s1 has 145393 standalone 5-digit numbers (dig5) and ZERO 5-digit tokens reach 201 occurrences. 145393/201 = 723.3, so at least ceil(145393/201) = 724 distinct values are required: a long tail, the signature of house numbers, not a bounded postal vocabulary (~41k US ZIPs in use, heavily concentrated at the top).
are_us_5_digit_values_house_numbers_or_z.consistent_with_already_settled: Consistent with the fleet brief's settled finding that no country has a postal field.

digit_ladder_train_s1.semantics: Occurrences of pure-digit address tokens WITHIN the top-4000 addr_tokens bag. TOKEN_RE = [a-z0-9]+. These are TOKEN OCCURRENCES, not rows.
digit_ladder_train_s1.caveat: Lower bounds only: top 4000 per country AND periodically pruned (prune() drops count<=1 every 8 chunks). The 5/6-digit zeros mean 'no value reached the cutoff', NOT 'no value exists'.
digit_ladder_train_s1.shape: Smooth decay past 4 digits and a hard cliff at 5, in both countries: the shape of a house/street-number field, not a postcode. India's 4-digit band collapses to 35 distinct values (11746 occ) while US keeps 553 (182654 occ).

derived_rates_train_s1.note: rate = field / by_country[c].rows, per build_profile.py. num_digits counts the ADDRESS only, not the name.

new_defect.title: US source-1 vs source-2/3 digit-free address asymmetry is ~60,000x, five orders of magnitude larger than the dig6 gap, and is undocumented

measured.metric: alpha_only_addr / rows (addresses containing no digit at all)
measured.headline: Exactly ONE digit-free US address in source-1, versus ~5-6% in sources 2/3. Reproduced independently in train and test.
measured.not_confined_to_6_digits: num_digits/row is 4.1667 (train_s1) vs 3.7514 (train_s2), so unlike the dig6 gap this is a whole-address difference.

new_defect.why_it_matters_INFERENCE: run_blocking.py:31 makes {split}_s1.parquet the blocking INDEX and s2+s3 the queries. A row with no address number generates no kind-2 (AA) key at all (keys.py:63 explodes nums, which is empty). At 0.0001% that is a non-issue for the index side, but the 5-6% of source-2/3 rows that are digit-free cannot be retrieved by an address-number key and depend entirely on the name-only key families (kinds 1, 3, 4). Direction of impact is query-side RECALL, not precision.
new_defect.why_no_recommendation: The brief's evidence standard forbids manufacturing a recommendation to look productive. I have NOT measured whether CAPS_NOADDR (keys.py:25) already covers these rows adequately. Flagged as measured and unexplained: source-1 and source-2/3 US addresses were apparently built by different pipelines, and nothing in the code or the profile documents that.

gaps: NOT MEASURABLE: how many France addresses BEGIN with a house number. build_profile.py:126-127 splits components then TOKEN_RE.findall each and Counter.update them, DESTROYING POSITION. addr_tokens is an unordered multiset. There is no positional field in the profile. GAP, not estimated.
NOT MEASURABLE: whether the house number sits in a consistent position relative to the street word. Same reason.

Consequence: the earlier "'STATE 5-digit' pattern occurs zero times" claim is POSITIONAL and therefore not reproducible from the profile. I do not repeat it as evidence; the counting argument in the .md section 4 replaces it and needs no position.
France train digit structure of any kind: data gap, unfixable from the provided files.
alpha_only_addr and num_digits were not queried for France test_s2/s3; only France test_s1 was needed for the 5-digit question.

field_semantics_from_build_profile_py.num_digits: digits in the ADDRESS only (line 114, sum over ba). Raw digit COUNT, not rows, not a name measure.
field_semantics_from_build_profile_py.dig5_dig6: lookaround-guarded regex (?<!\d)\d{5}(?!\d) and (?<!\d)\d{6}(?!\d), lines 29-30. A digit inside a longer digit run does NOT count.
field_semantics_from_build_profile_py.has_digit_name: separate ROW count, any digit in business_name (line 106). This is the digit-in-NAME field.
field_semantics_from_build_profile_py.alpha_only_addr: rows where the address is non-empty and contains no digit at all (lines 117-118).
field_semantics_from_build_profile_py.per_country_stats: totals across the whole slice; all rates derived by dividing by that country's rows.
field_semantics_from_build_profile_py.name_tokens_addr_tokens: top 4000 per country AND periodically pruned (prune(), PRUNE_EVERY=8), so counts are lower bounds. Absence means 'did not reach the top 4000', never 'does not occur'.
field_semantics_from_build_profile_py.flattening: ADDR_SPLIT=[,;] then TOKEN_RE per component (lines 126-127), so a token count is not automatically a pipeline-visible quantity AND position is lost.

denominator_warning: ANY France rate computed against a train-file France denominator is meaningless. This is the exact error that produced the retracted '100% of France rows resolve a state' figure. Check the denominator before accepting any France train statistic.
